## Overview

Add opt-in filesystem KV-offload I/O deadlines while retaining primary buffers until physical I/O completion. Implements Item 2 of #54363; related lifecycle work: #61667.

## Claims

- `io_timeout_seconds: float | None = None` uses monotonic submission deadlines and preserves the default behavior.
- Expired loads become misses while their destination slots remain quarantined; expired stores retain their source pins. Late completion releases resources without reporting a second logical result.
- Physical inflight accounting remains valid through cancellation, drain, reset, and shutdown. New promotions/cascades to a tier pause while timed-out I/O remains unfinished.
- FS deadlines do not change object-storage or P2P protocol behavior, file formats, checksums, cleanup, or retry policies.

## Validation

Environment: Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu; native `fs_io_C` built from the unchanged source. Both Python fallback and native I/O variants executed.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused FS/tiering/metrics tests | 147 passed |
| Tiering, CPU manager/shared-region, offloading connector regressions | 1264 passed, 3 skipped |
| Same-key recomputation followed by late old I/O | Passed |
| Shutdown negative control using upstream thread pool | Fails as expected; fixed implementation passes |
| Repository pre-commit checks, including Ruff and mypy | Passed |
| GPU serving/model evaluation and serving performance benchmark | Not run; CPU-only environment |

The three skips are the unavailable optional `kvcr` package and two empty worker-backend parameter sets. Event-controlled tests cover deadline equality, completion races, queued cancellation, late physical completion, slot non-reuse, physical inflight counts, and reset/shutdown safety.

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_shared_offload_region.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector -q

git diff --name-only -z upstream/main...HEAD |
  xargs -0 .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files
```

**Outstanding validation:** the human submitter must run and record serving end-to-end validation and relevant model evaluation before publication, as required by the repository's contribution policy and `/pr-checklist`. CPU lifecycle tests do not establish GPU serving behavior. Update the results above after validation; no performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

A filesystem syscall may block indefinitely while accessing a primary KV buffer. Returning an ordinary failed completion would allow the allocator to reuse that buffer too early. The manager therefore separates one-time logical failure from physical resource release. Promotions detach failed keys but retain the slot IDs; cascades retain read pins. A late result only releases the retained resources. Primary read/write occupancy remains charged throughout retention.

Pool cancellation and worker start share a condition lock. Never-started jobs are canceled through an index and skipped by workers; running jobs remain physically inflight until they return. Completion is acknowledged under the pool lock, so a result published at or after its deadline is conservatively treated as expired. Timeouts are observed at the next manager poll.

Blocked syscalls cannot be forcibly canceled safely. This PR adds no per-block cancellation to either I/O path: running batches may continue, and drain/reset/shutdown can wait indefinitely. Native tests execute real I/O after a controlled delay; they do not emulate an indefinitely stalled NFS/FUSE syscall.

Duplicate check on 2026-10-16, against upstream `642c18d64c`: issue discussion, open issue-reference/area searches and recent merged history found no overlapping FS deadline implementation. #57912 covers checksums and #61780 covers failed-store backpressure. Recheck these searches before submission.

#61667 covers P2P consumer lifetime. This change aligns the small primary quarantine API with that proposal, but shared manager/metrics changes still need reconciliation according to merge order. No P2P transport/session changes are included. The common-layer changes are limited to deadline decisions, buffer ownership and accounting; OBJ deadline integration is deferred.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, independent source review, and local test execution. The human submitter remains responsible for understanding and reviewing every changed line and rerunning relevant tests.

@@ -191,11 +191,18 @@ The filesystem tier (`type: "fs"`) writes blocks to a filesystem directory.
 | `root_dir` | yes | — | Base directory; vLLM creates subdirectories beneath it (see [On-Disk Layout](#on-disk-layout)). |
 | `n_read_threads` | no | `16` | Read-priority I/O threads (load path). |
 | `n_write_threads` | no | `16` | Write-priority I/O threads (store path). |
+| `io_timeout_seconds` | no | `null` | Finite positive deadline in seconds, measured from submission; expired jobs fail when the scheduler next polls the tier. |
 | `enable_kv_events` | no | `false` | Publish `BlockStored` KV events (medium `STORAGE`) for successfully stored blocks. Requires KV cache events to be enabled globally. |
 | `locality` | no | unspecified | `LOCAL` or `REMOTE` relative to the publishing vLLM instance. Included in the tier's KV events only when explicitly configured. |
 
 Each thread group prefers its own queue but pulls from the other when its primary queue is empty, so a write-heavy or read-heavy burst won't leave the off-priority queue waiting. Size the totals to your storage's effective concurrency.
 
+When `io_timeout_seconds` is set, the tiering manager reports an expired job as failed without waiting for its filesystem I/O to return. Primary-tier slots remain reserved until the worker actually finishes, so late I/O cannot access a reused slot. No extra block buffer is allocated. A blocked filesystem syscall still occupies its worker thread and primary-tier slots until it returns.
+
+While any timed-out I/O remains unfinished, new promotions and cascades to that filesystem tier are skipped; they resume after all such I/O completes. Other tiers and GPU recomputation remain available, subject to primary-tier capacity. The timeout counter is `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_io_timeouts{tier,direction}`; primary read/write usage gauges continue to include the retained slots.
+
+`drain_jobs()`, cache reset, and shutdown still wait for physical completion and can block indefinitely on a stuck syscall. Completion is acknowledged under the pool lock, so a result published at or after the deadline is conservatively treated as timed out even if the syscall returned slightly earlier.
+
 #### On-Disk Layout
 
 Under `root_dir`, vLLM creates a subdirectory `<model>_<digest>`, where `<model>` is the model name with `/` replaced by `_` (so HuggingFace IDs like `meta-llama/Llama-3-8B` don't nest), and `<digest>` is a short SHA256 prefix derived from the run configuration (model, block size, parallelism, dtype, etc.). Runs with the same configuration share the same subdirectory; runs with different configurations live side-by-side under the same `root_dir` without colliding.

+    keys = [key(1)]
+    prepared = primary.prepare_write(keys, _CTX)
+    assert prepared is not None
+    slot = int(prepared.store_spec.chunk_ids[0])
+    tensor[slot].fill_(7)
+    path = tier.file_mapper.get_file_name(keys[0])
+    if is_promotion:

+    else:

+        primary.prepare_read(keys, _CTX)

+    if expire:
+        job.submit_time -= 61
+    started, release = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
+    operation = "batch_load_block" if is_promotion else "batch_store_block"
+    batch = getattr(io_mod, operation)
+
+    def blocked_batch(*args):
+        started.set()
+        assert release.wait(10)
+        batch(*args)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        "vllm.v1.kv_offload.tiering.fs.manager." + operation, blocked_batch
+    )
+    manager._register_job(job, 0)
+    submit = tier.submit_load if is_promotion else tier.submit_store
+    submit(job)
+    try:
+        assert started.wait(5)
+        manager._process_finished_jobs()
+        assert tier._pool._inflight_jobs == 1
+        if expire:
+            assert not manager._jobs
+            assert manager._timed_out_jobs
+            assert slot not in primary._free_list
+            assert not manager._should_store_to_tier(tier, 1)

+            manager._processed_jobs_this_step = False
+            assert manager.lookup(key(99), _CTX) is LookupResult.MISS
+            tier.lookup.assert_not_called()
+        if is_promotion:
+            assert primary._num_write_pending_chunks == 1
+        else:

+        manager._process_finished_jobs()

+        assert not manager.has_pending_work()

+        if is_promotion:
+            assert torch.all(tensor[slot] == 7)
+            assert primary._num_write_pending_chunks == 0
+            expected = LookupResult.MISS if expire else LookupResult.HIT
+            assert primary.lookup(keys[0], _CTX) is expected
+            assert primary._free_list.count(slot) == int(expire)
+        else:

+def test_shutdown_counts_only_physically_finished_jobs():
+    """Cancel queued tasks without declaring the running task memory-safe."""
+    pool = DualQueueThreadPool(1, 0)
+    started, release = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
+    idle, checked = threading.Event(), threading.Event()
+    canceled_ran = threading.Event()
+
+    def blocked():
+        started.set()
+        assert release.wait(10)
+
+    pool.enqueue_load(1, 2, [blocked, canceled_ran.set])
+    assert started.wait(5)
+    pool.enqueue_store(2, 1, [canceled_ran.set])
+    original_wait_for = pool._condition.wait_for
+
+    def observed_wait_for(predicate):
+        def observed_predicate():
+            result = predicate()
+            checked.set()
+            return result
+
+        return original_wait_for(observed_predicate)
+
+    pool._condition.wait_for = observed_wait_for

+        release.set()
+        pool.shutdown(wait=True)
+        waiter.join(5)
+        assert idle.is_set()

💬 Join our developer Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai to discuss your PR in `#pr-reviews`, coordinate on features in `#feat-` channels, or join special interest groups in `#sig-` channels.

PRs do not trigger a full CI run by default. Reviewers with write access and configured trusted contributors can comment `/ci run` for upstream CI or `/amd-ci run` for AMD CI only whenever CI signals are needed.

Once the PR is approved or has the `ready` label, the PR author can also use the corresponding `/ci run`, `/ci retry`, and `/ci cancel` commands, or their `/amd-ci` variants. New commits do not start upstream CI automatically.
